points: skin → nodules, livedo racemosa, ulcers, digital gangrene.

**Skin (~25–60%):** **tender subcutaneous nodules (0.5–2 cm) along arteries** of the lower legs/thighs; **livedo racemosa** (feet, legs); **punched-out ulcers** (D02 — sensitive); digital ischaemia; "starburst" livedo around nodules.
deep **incisional skin biopsy of a nodule to subcutis** (medium artery with fibrinoid necrosis; DIF non-specific), or **muscle/sural nerve biopsy** guided by symptoms/EMG.
**CT/MR angiography or catheter angiography** — **microaneurysms** and stenoses of renal/mesenteric/hepatic arteries ("arteriographic abnormality").

**French Vasculitis Study Group predictive items (Henegar 2008; course list):** positive — **HBsAg+, arteriographic abnormalities, mono/polyneuropathy**; negative — **ANCA, asthma, ENT signs, glomerulopathy, cryoglobulinaemia**.

**Severity — revised Five-Factor Score (FFS 2011)** for PAN: age >65, cardiac insufficiency, GI involvement, renal insufficiency (creatinine ≥150 µmol/L). Each = 1 point; ≥1 point = worse prognosis → cyclophosphamide added.

items.t: Foot drop or new numbness, severe abdominal pain or testicular pain with nodules or livedo: **urgent** referral for systemic PAN.

pearls.t: "**Nodules + livedo + neuropathy + hypertension, ANCA negative → think PAN, and check hepatitis B.**"
PAN **spares glomeruli**. Haematuria with red-cell casts points to ANCA vasculitis.
Hepatitis B serology **before** starting steroids/immunosuppressants for any vasculitis (reactivation risk) — this applies to rituximab especially.
